scenes.tts: Each receptor reports on its own patch. So how does the eye mark an edge? Neighbours compare.
scenes.visual: Title card: Neighbours Compare. A light-dark edge across a row of receptor units.
scenes.narration: Each receptor reports on its own patch. So how does the eye mark an edge? Neighbours compare.

scenes.tts: The horseshoe crab, Limulus, has a compound eye. Each unit, an ommatidium, sends its own fibre into the optic nerve.
scenes.visual: A horseshoe crab, then a close-up of its lateral eye as a grid of ommatidia. One ommatidium highlighted with its own fibre running into the optic nerve. Labels: Limulus, ommatidium.
scenes.narration: The horseshoe crab, Limulus, has a compound eye. Each unit, an ommatidium, sends its own fibre into the optic nerve.

scenes.tts: Hartline, Wagner and Ratliff recorded one ommatidium. Steady light gave a steady discharge.
scenes.visual: A microelectrode in one ommatidium. A firing-rate meter holds steady under a constant spot of light. Label: Hartline, Wagner and Ratliff, 1956.
scenes.narration: Hartline, Wagner and Ratliff recorded one ommatidium. Steady light gave a steady discharge.

scenes.tts: Then they lit its neighbours as well. The discharge fell.
scenes.visual: Light spreads to the surrounding ommatidia. The recorded unit's rate meter drops.
scenes.narration: Then they lit its neighbours as well. The discharge fell.

scenes.tts: Was that the circuit at work? Or just stray light inside the eye?
scenes.visual: On-screen question: circuit, or stray light? The two options shown as icons: connections between units, and scattered light rays.
scenes.narration: Was that the circuit at work? Or just stray light inside the eye?

scenes.tts: They cut the lateral connections to the recorded unit. The neighbours' light no longer inhibited it. The inhibition ran through connections between units.
scenes.visual: Scissors cut the lateral connections around the recorded ommatidium. The neighbours stay lit, but the rate meter recovers to its steady level. Label: inhibition needs the connections.
scenes.narration: They cut the lateral connections to the recorded unit. The neighbours' light no longer inhibited it. The inhibition ran through connections between units.

scenes.tts: Think of each unit as reporting its own light, minus a share of its neighbours' light.
scenes.visual: One unit with arrows from its two neighbours. On screen: output = own light minus a share of neighbours' light.
scenes.narration: Think of each unit as reporting its own light, minus a share of its neighbours' light.

scenes.tts: Now take a row of units at an edge, dim on the left and bright on the right. The row continues beyond both ends. The numbers stay on screen.
scenes.visual: A cropped segment of six bars for input: 10, 10, 10, 20, 20, 20, with continuation marks and a dim ghost neighbour on the left and a bright ghost neighbour on the right. Below, an empty output row. On screen: output = own − 0.2 × (left + right). Label: made-up units; feedforward toy model; row continues. The numbers are shown, not spoken.
scenes.narration: Now take a row of units at an edge, dim on the left and bright on the right. The row continues beyond both ends. The numbers stay on screen.

scenes.tts: Deep inside each uniform region, every unit is inhibited by neighbours just like itself. Both plateaus drop.
scenes.visual: The interior output bars fill in: 6 on the dim side, 12 on the bright side. The two edge positions stay empty.
scenes.narration: Deep inside each uniform region, every unit is inhibited by neighbours just like itself. Both plateaus drop.

scenes.tts: Now the dim unit right beside the edge. One of its neighbours is bright. Will it sit above its plateau, or below?
scenes.visual: The dim edge unit flashes with a question mark. On-screen question: above or below the dim plateau?
scenes.narration: Now the dim unit right beside the edge. One of its neighbours is bright. Will it sit above its plateau, or below?

scenes.tts: Below. Its bright neighbour inhibits it more. And the bright unit at the edge sits above its plateau, because one neighbour is dim.
scenes.visual: The edge bars fill in: 4 on the dim side, dipping below 6; 14 on the bright side, rising above 12. Arrows show stronger inhibition from the bright neighbour and weaker inhibition from the dim one.
scenes.narration: Below. Its bright neighbour inhibits it more. And the bright unit at the edge sits above its plateau, because one neighbour is dim.

scenes.tts: What changed? The step across the edge is the same size as the input step.
scenes.visual: A bracket compares the step across the edge: 10 in, and 10 out (14 against 4). The bracket stays on screen.
scenes.narration: What changed? The step across the edge is the same size as the input step.

scenes.tts: But the uniform regions now differ less. So the edge stands out against them.
scenes.visual: A second bracket compares the plateaus: 10 apart in, 6 apart out. Contrast values appear: 0.33 in, 0.33 for the plateaus, 0.56 across the edge. Text: the edge keeps its size; the plateaus move closer; contrast at the edge rises.
scenes.narration: But the uniform regions now differ less. So the edge stands out against them.

scenes.tts: The full model of the crab eye uses each neighbour's output, and the result still holds. In the vertebrate retina, other cells build the surround.
scenes.visual: The row redraws with arrows from each unit's output to its neighbours, and the edge pattern survives with a small ripple. Then a small inset of a vertebrate retina, label: surrounds built by other cells.
scenes.narration: The full model of the crab eye uses each neighbour's output, and the result still holds. In the vertebrate retina, other cells build the surround.

scenes.tts: Lateral inhibition discounts uniform regions, so differences stand out. Neighbours compare.
scenes.visual: The output row glows at the edge. Text: lateral inhibition discounts uniform regions, so the edge stands out.
scenes.narration: Lateral inhibition discounts uniform regions, so differences stand out. Neighbours compare.
